articles.title: Dolly Parton Net Worth: How did the country singer build his fortune?
articles.standfirst: Dolly Parton's net worth is a reflection of her diverse ventures
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's net worth is a reflection of her diverse ventures
articles.body:
D olly Parton, the legendary country icon, was not just a musical powerhouse; she's a financial force to be reckoned with.

With a net worth of $650 million, Parton's wealth is a testament to her multifaceted career spanning music, acting, songwriting, and business ventures .

Whitney Houston's impact in Parton's income

At the heart of her financial empire is the iconic song "I Will Always Love You," a hit that topped the Billboard country music chart in March 1974.

While widely perceived as a love song, Parton originally penned it as a farewell to her professional partner, Porter Wagoner.

Several reports state that the song has generated over $20 million in royalties for Parton, showcasing its enduring popularity.

Whitney Houston's 1992 cover of the song for "The Bodyguard" soundtrack propelled it to new heights, spending 14 weeks atop the Billboard chart.

Parton, reflecting on Houston's rendition, invested some of the song's earnings in a Nashville neighborhood, emphasizing her connection to Whitney's legacy.

Parton's song catalog has over 3 thousand songs

Parton's financial success extends beyond "I Will Always Love You."

With 41 top-10 country albums, 25 No. 1 singles, and over 100 million solo albums sold, she continues to be a dominant force in the music industry.

Her entire song catalog, which is said to contain more than 3 thousand songs, is estimated to be worth more than $150 million.

Parton's estimated annual income, mostly coming from her song royalties is said to be over $85 million.

Owning her life's work has been a strategic move for Parton since launching her music publishing company in 1966.

Dolly Parton's net worth is a reflection of her diverse ventures.

Beyond music, she has excelled in acting, with roles in classics like "9 to 5" and "Steel Magnolias."

Her business acumen extends to fragrance, with "Scent From Above," and the famed amusement park, Dollywood.

Dolly Parton passed away at 80

The legendary country singer and songwriter Dolly Parton has died this tuesday August 25 at the age of 80 , according to a statement released by her family.

The news was shared on Instagram by her nephew, Brian Seaver , who reflected on the profound loss. “I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it until now,” he said, describing it as both a tremendous honour filled with pride and a moment of deep sadness.

articles.title: Carrot Top Net Worth: The Las Vegas residency that changed everything
articles.standfirst: The comedian built a business model around consistency and fans love him for that
articles.summary: The comedian built a business model around consistency and fans love him for that
articles.body:
Carrot Top has been one of the most recognizable faces in comedy. Known for his bright red hair, energetic performances and signature prop-based routines, the comedian has built a career that has endured far longer than many of his peers. Along the way, he has also amassed a sizable fortune, one that has a surprisingly strong connection to Las Vegas.

According to estimates from Celebrity Net Worth, Carrot Top, whose real name is Scott Thompson, has a net worth of approximately $70 million. The outlet also estimates that he earns around $8 million annually through his various professional ventures. While those figures have not been publicly confirmed by Thompson , they offer a glimpse into the financial success of one of stand-up comedy’s most enduring performers.

The foundation of that success can be traced to a decision that transformed him from a touring comedian into a Las Vegas institution. Since 2005, Carrot Top has headlined his own show at the Luxor Hotel and Casino , making his residency one of the longest-running comedy engagements on the Las Vegas Strip.

While many comedians rely on extensive national tours, television projects or streaming specials to maintain visibility, Carrot Top built a business model around consistency. Night after night, year after year, audiences continued to fill seats to see the comedian’s unique blend of stand-up and elaborate props.

A longevity that has proven invaluable

That longevity has proven invaluable. Las Vegas residencies have long been associated with music superstars, but Carrot Top demonstrated that a comedian could also become a destination attraction. Over two decades, the Luxor show became a cornerstone of his career and a significant contributor to his financial success.

His rise to fame began in the 1990s, when his inventive use of props helped him stand out in a crowded comedy landscape. While some critics initially viewed the style as a novelty, audiences embraced it, and Carrot Top steadily expanded his profile through television appearances and film projects.

Over the years, he appeared on popular shows including Scrubs, George Lopez and Last Comic Standing. More recently, he made a cameo as himself in the acclaimed Max comedy series Hacks in 2024 . Those appearances helped keep his name in the public eye, but none matched the consistency of his Las Vegas residency.

Recent news surrounding the comedian has resonated strongly

Thompson was recently hospitalized and is receiving medical care and support, according to statements from his representative. His family has requested privacy as he continues his recovery. The news has prompted renewed interest in the comedian’s lengthy career and legacy.

For many fans, Carrot Top is more than a performer who enjoyed a brief moment of popularity. He is a rare example of a comedian who successfully reinvented himself from a television-era personality into a permanent fixture of America’s entertainment capital.

Few comedians can claim to have remained a headline act in the same city for more than 20 years. Even fewer can point to a residency that became synonymous with their personal brand. In Carrot Top’s case, Las Vegas was not simply another stop on a tour schedule, it became the center of a comedy empire.

articles.title: Susan Dell Net Worth: Wife of Dell Technologies founder has been there every step of the way with Michael Dell
articles.standfirst: The CEO of Dell has amassed an incredible fortune with his wife right by his side.
articles.summary: The CEO of Dell has amassed an incredible fortune with his wife right by his side.
articles.body:
Like any major company, Dell once started as just an idea. Michael Dell realized in the mid-1980s that selling PCs directly to consumers was a better business strategy than traditional retail processes. Along the way, he turned Dell into one of the biggest companies in the world. His wife, Susan Dell , was with him nearly every step of the way.

Michael married Susan Lieberman in 1989 , five years after Dell had officially founded " Dell Computer Corporation ". By the early 1990s, Dell was already a rising force in the tech industry. When Michael and Susan married in 1989, not even they could have imagined where they would end up 37 years later.

Michael Dell is the fourth-richest person in the world, according to Forbes

According to Forbes , Michael Dell currently has a net worth of $282.5 billion . That makes him the fourth-richest person in the entire world . There is currently no public record or verifiable evidence that Michael and Susan signed any kind of prenuptial and postnuptial agreement . That means Dell's net worth also applies to Susan . If they were to ever get divorced, she would be entitled to half of it, although legal proceedings would be extensive given the incredible amount of money at stake.

Susan has helped Michael use a lot of his money for good. In 1999, they established the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation , which they've used for philanthropic causes related to education and health. Most recently, the Dells donated $6.25 billion to "Trump accounts" , which are investment accounts for young children. The expectation is that $250 will be provided to 25 million children in need .

Given that Dell struck a $9.7 billion deal with the U.S. military to provide software in 2026 , the company is only growing as Michael and Susan get older. Their four children are set to inherit most of it once they pass.

articles.title: Allen Bailey Net Worth: Former Chiefs player spent a decade as an NFL veteran
articles.standfirst: Bailey carved out a long career in the NFL as a third round pick in 2011.
articles.summary: Bailey carved out a long career in the NFL as a third round pick in 2011.
articles.body:
The football world is in mourning on Wednesday, following the news that former NFL defensive end Allen Bailey has passed away at the age of 37 .

Bailey's death was confirmed to TMZ by his brother, Alford Bailey Jr. He was reportedly found deceased on Tuesday in his Florida home by his wife. It's believed he died of natural causes .

Bailey was a third round pick out of the University of Miami in 2011 . He was a constant on the Miami Hurricanes defense, racking up 31 tackles for loss and 19 sacks over his last three seasons in college.

Allen Bailey played eight seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs and two seasons with the Atlanta Falcons

The defensive end parlayed that into becoming the 86th overall pick in the 2011 NFL Draft . The Kansas City Chiefs selected him, and he went on to repay them by spending eight seasons with the organization as a role player at first, then as a full-time starter a few years into his career.

Bailey finished out his NFL career with the Atlanta Falcons , where he spent his last two seasons before being released in 2021 . He never formally announced his retirement, but instead quietly put a bow on a solid NFL career .

Bailey did well for himself and his family, earning $38.123 million over the course of his professional career, per Spotrac . There aren't many records of investments or brand partnerships that Bailey took part in, therefore his final estimated net worth is unknown.

articles.title: Martha Firestone Ford's Net Worth: What was the net worth of the owner and president emerita of the Detroit Lions at the time of her death at age 101?
articles.standfirst: Estimates of the late NFL matriarch’s personal fortune ranged from $800 million to $1.4 billion
articles.summary: Estimates of the late NFL matriarch’s personal fortune ranged from $800 million to $1.4 billion
articles.body:
When Martha Firestone Ford died peacefully at age 101 on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at her home in Grosse Pointe Shores, Michigan, she left behind an extraordinary chapter in American business and professional football.

As the link between two iconic industrial dynasties and the longtime matriarch of the Detroit Lions , Ford ranked among the wealthiest figures in the NFL, though the exact value of her personal estate at the time of her passing has not been publicly disclosed.

Because private family holdings and trust structures are rarely itemized in public filings, financial trackers have offered differing snapshots of her fortune over the years.

In its 2019 historical billionaire profile, Forbes estimated Ford’s net worth at $1.4 billion, identifying her stake in Ford Motor Company as the cornerstone of her wealth alongside her ownership interest in the Lions.

By contrast, Celebrity Net Worth has placed her fortune closer to $800 million, noting that its estimate relies on publicly available records rather than audited financial statements.

That $600 million gap underscores why neither figure can be treated as a definitive accounting of her estate in 2026, particularly since team valuations reflect enterprise equity rather than liquid cash on hand.

Ford’s financial standing was rooted in an unmatched industrial pedigree. Born Martha Parke Firestone in Cleveland, Ohio, in September 1925, she was the granddaughter of Firestone Tire and Rubber Company founder Harvey Firestone.

In 1947, she married William Clay Ford Sr. , a grandson of automotive pioneer Henry Ford and a longtime executive at Ford Motor Company, uniting two of the twentieth century’s defining manufacturing fortunes.

How six decades of Detroit Lions ownership and Ford family leadership shaped her legacy

Beyond her automotive and tire heritage, Ford’s name became synonymous with Detroit football. She and William Clay Ford Sr. acquired full control of the Detroit Lions in 1963 for roughly $4.5 million, beginning a family stewardship that has now spanned more than six decades.

Following her husband’s death in March 2014, Ford stepped forward at age 88 to assume sole control as principal owner and chairwoman, guiding the organization for six seasons, a tenure highlighted by postseason appearances in 2014 and 2016 as well as a privately financed $100 million renovation of Ford Field in 2017.

In June 2020, Ford handed principal ownership duties to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp , while transitioning into an emeritus leadership role and remaining a fixture on the sidelines into her second century.

By September 2026, Forbes valued the Detroit Lions at approximately $8.04 billion, illustrating how dramatically the franchise appreciated even after day-to-day control passed to the next generation.

Ford is survived by her four children, Sheila Ford Hamp , Martha Ford Morse, Ford Motor Company executive chairman William Clay Ford Jr., and Elizabeth Ford Kontulis , along with 14 grandchildren and 17 great-grandchildren.

While the family has not shared details regarding how her personal assets will be distributed, her enduring civic impact across metro Detroit, including decades of service on the Henry Ford Health System board and helping establish the Maplegrove Center, was front and center in the Lions’ official tribute: “She cared so deeply about her family, the players, their fans, and the city of Detroit. She was committed to making the Lions - and the game of football - better.”
